{{Recipe}}

Miyan gyada is a traditional Nigerian soup popular in northern Nigeria, especially among the Hausa people.

It is made from groundnuts (peanuts), which are blended into a paste and cooked to form a rich, creamy [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]]. The dish is usually prepared with meat or fish, vegetables, and local spices, giving it a deep, nutty flavor.

Miyan gyada has a thick, smooth texture and is highly nutritious and filling. It is commonly served with northern swallows like tuwo shinkafa or tuwo dawa and is an important part of northern Nigerian cuisine.

== Ingredients ==

* 500 g [[Cookbook:Meat|meat]] or [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]]
* 1 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Dehydrated Broth|seasoning cubes]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Peanut|groundnuts/peanuts]] or groundnut paste
* 3–4 [[Cookbook:Scotch Bonnet Chile|Scotch bonnet peppers]]
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|palm oil]] or [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 2 cups leafy vegetables (e.g. [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]] or [[Cookbook:Fluted Pumpkin|ugu]] leaf)

* 4–5 cups water or meat [[Cookbook:Broth and Stock|stock]]
* 2 medium [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] (optional)

== Procedure ==

# Season with onions, salt, and seasoning cubes, then [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] until tender. Keep the stock.
# Blend groundnuts (or use ready paste) until smooth.
# Add the paste into the pot and allow it to cook, stirring to prevent burning.
# Add pepper and a little palm oil or vegetable oil, then mix well.
# Add your leafy vegetables and stir.
# Allow the soup to cook until it thickens and oil begins to rise to the top. The soup should be thick, creamy, and rich with a nutty flavor.
# Taste and add salt or seasoning if needed.
# Serve with swallows like tuwo shinkafa or Tuwo dawa.
